name: Columnar Basalt
desc: Looking straight down on a cooling lava sheet that has cracked itself into hexagons — column tops sit at their own heights as ball-and-socket plateaus, vesicles pit the rind, chipped rubble wedges into the joints, and a low raking sun crawls around the pavement while a wet front sheets across and dries away behind it; weathered causeway, hard-broken quarry stone, moonlit basalt, false-colour relief or a hatched survey plate.

energy.doc: relief gain and tonal contrast — max lights the columns hard and drives the joints black

scale.doc: magnification of the pavement — max nearly triples column size, a true macro zoom (grain magnifies with it)

density.doc: column count — 0 is a coarse colonnade of few fat columns, 1 a fine entablature of many

speed.doc: rate of joint creep and the sweep of the wet front (0.2 still reorganises)

wet.doc: how much water sheets the rock — darkens the stone and turns the specular on

weather.doc: weathering rind: oxidation mottle, vesicle pitting and joint bloom over cold fresh basalt

hue.doc: hue of the oxidised weathering rind (cold grey basalt shows through underneath)

style.doc: aesthetic: weathered wet sea-cliff causeway / hard-broken dry quarry basalt in blue-grey / moonlit near-monochrome wet pavement / false-colour normal-and-height relief with no rock at all / geological survey plate as pure joint line and stipple on cream

seed.doc: deterministic seed for the lattice jitter, column heights and ball-or-socket tops
